title: Reorder List
prompt:
You are given the `head` of a singly linked list containing `n` nodes. Reorder the list in place so that the nodes alternate between the front and back of the original order: node 0, then node n-1, then node 1, then node n-2, then node 2, and so on. You must do this by rewiring the existing nodes (not by creating new ones or simply reordering values in an array).

The list is given as an array (e.g. `[1,2,3,4]` represents `1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> null`). The starter code includes helpers to convert between the array and a linked-list node — build the actual list, rewire it, then convert back to an array to return.
constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [1, 5 * 10^4]
hints: Find the middle of the list using slow/fast pointers, then reverse the second half.
Once you have two halves — the first half in original order and the second half reversed — the answer is just weaving them together node by node.
Be careful to terminate the merged list properly: the last node's `next` must be set to null, otherwise you can create an accidental cycle.

solution.approach: Split the list into two halves using slow/fast pointers (slow ends at the midpoint). Reverse the second half in place. Then merge the two halves by alternating nodes: take one from the first half, one from the second, and so on, relinking `next` pointers as you go. Terminate the final node with null.
